narrative: Material PL1__M3E92184 shows erratic demand (CV=0.77) with 75.7% active working days and a Gamma-like distribution driven by high day-to-day variability. Lead times are short (mean 1.36 days) but moderately variable (CV=0.59). The (r,Q) continuous-review policy was selected because erratic but not intermittent demand benefits from a fixed reorder point that triggers replenishment deterministically, while EOQ consolidates the previously excessive ordering frequency from ~751 to ~45 orders/year. Safety stock is reduced from SAP's 4,125 to 3,392 units, correctly calibrated to the 95% service level.
warnings: Lead time CV=0.59 classified as moderate; monitor for further volatility.
Demand has 24.3% zero-demand days — erratic pattern requires regular review of reorder point.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Erratic but non-intermittent demand (75.7% active days, CV=0.77) with short lead times suits a continuous-review (r,Q) policy. The EOQ significantly exceeds MOQ, making batch consolidation the primary lever. Fixed order quantity simplifies procurement and aligns with supplier MOQ constraints.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage utilization at 63.8% (14,383/22,553 units) — capacity is not binding. If demand surges or safety stock is raised, the remaining 8,170 units of headroom provides adequate buffer.
